The private version runs locally. A lightweight JSON-to-LaTeX renderer is still used to generate tailored cover letters, while the broader tracker direction continues separately in AAAAT.

header.title: AI workflows
header.subtitle: LLM workflows, tool integration, automation, developer tooling, and technical documentation.

paragraphs: My AI-related work is concentrated on the software around model use: structured inputs and outputs, tool calls, state, local data, validation, and integration with scripts or repository workflows.

AgenticCareerBoost is the main public example because it combines these model-facing pieces with ordinary engineering artifacts: JSON content, Python and shell tooling, GitHub Actions, LaTeX, static pages, and application utilities.

header.label: FOCUS / BACKEND
header.title: Backend and tooling
header.subtitle: Java/Spring base, domain rules, technical documentation, and platform-oriented work.

paragraphs: This view is for backend/platform conversations about behavior, boundaries, tooling, and maintainability. Java/Spring is part of the route, not the whole identity.
I am most interested in backend work when the domain has real shape: rules, transitions, permissions, failures, and enough complexity to reward clear structure.

IronBank shows the Java/Spring baseline. P3CTeX shows tooling and document-engineering depth. AAAAT extends the local application-tooling thread. AgenticCareerBoost combines several of these concerns in one repository through static content, scripts, CI, reports, and local utilities.
